## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-10-27] The paper-trader bought Leidos on 10-26 as a name with "no AI-capex… overlap". But Burry's Palantir short thesis, which Fred holds a live put on, says Palantir is the same kind of business as Leidos: engineers deployed on site to wire software into government systems. Together with the live Accenture long, the book is making a relative-value bet that integrators' multiples will converge, and nothing in it says so.** [[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-10-26-LDOS]] thesis point 4 calls LDOS a diversifier because it isn't on Burry's short list (which includes PLTR). [[finance/short-research/source-burry-palantir-new-clothes-2026-02-12]] argues Palantir is "fundamentally a consultancy". On his reading, its Forward-Deployed Engineers integrate clients' existing SAP/Oracle/Accenture systems for months at a time, and the company is priced like SaaS only because that labour is booked outside cost of goods sold. [[ai-tech/source-palantir-nvidia-nemotron-2026-07-02]] gives the bull version: Palantir as the government's model-agnostic "trusted intermediary" for AI. That is the role a defence IT integrator like Leidos sells, and DoD units are already routing Nemotron work through Palantir. [[finance/trading-portfolio]] holds the PLTR put (≈€310) next to ACN (+57%, the commercial version of the same model). So LDOS and PLTR sit on opposite sides of one question: does government AI spending go to the integrator priced at 11x guidance or to the one priced as software? The put and LDOS/ACN pay off in the same scenario, a re-rating of Palantir toward a consultancy multiple. In the other scenario, where Palantir takes share, both lose. One more risk applies to LDOS and ACN but not to PLTR: AI deflation of billable hours. [[technology/source-salesforce-agentic-engineering-2026]] reports a migration estimated at 231 person-days finished in 13 days with Claude Code. That is the billable-hours base of a services integrator, and the AI-risk table's bubble-only test (09-29 connection) misses it again here. **Check at LDOS's Q3 (~Nov 3) and ACN's next print:** look for any mention of Palantir as a competitor or partner, and whether fixed-price or AI-delivered work is compressing headcount-linked revenue.

No new investigation ideas; no older items resolved; no new podcast books.

## New investigation ideas

- **[2026-10-26] Fred's growth-vs-value tracker measures only US style indexes, but his live book is mostly European value, and this week's Swedroe piece says Europe is exactly where the value case is weakest.** [[finance/market-growth-vs-value]] tracks seven US ETFs (QQQ, IWF, SPY, IWD, IVE, IWM, IWN). Today's run reports value leading by −2,234 bps, a new 2026 high, and that is easy to read as a tailwind for the live book. But [[finance/trading-portfolio]] holds six EUR names (SAP, EDEN, ACN, PRX, WKL, ZOE) plus three UK ones (KLR, GSK, REL), and none of them sits in any index the tracker follows. [[finance/morningstar/source-morningstar-swedroe-valuation-spreads-2026-10-23]] puts the AQR large-cap value spread at the 80th percentile in the US, 62nd in emerging markets, and only the 42nd (below average) in developed international markets. Its own Portfolio Relevance line already says the European tilt is where spreads are least wide, but nothing has carried that into the tracker or the briefing. So the tracker's headline is measuring a premium Fred mostly doesn't own. **Next step:** add one non-US style pair to the growth-value tracker's ticker list, for example EFV/EFG (iShares MSCI EAFE Value/Growth) or a Europe-only value ETF if yfinance prices it cleanly, and report its spread next to IWD/IWF. If the European spread is flat or favours growth while the US one widens, the briefing's "value is working" reading does not apply to most of the live book. That matters for the open EDEN and PRX Exit decisions, which currently lean on "value rotation" as background support.

## New cross-domain connections

- **[2026-10-26] The bitcoin miners' pivot to AI hosting, which the paper book traded as a growth story in July, has turned them into creditors of the weakest borrowers in AI. This week's CoreWeave bond crash shows the risk, and Crypto has never connected bitcoin's miner base to neocloud credit.** [[finance/paper-trading-vol/trades/2026-07-15-CLSK]] bought CleanSpark because the market was "rewarding richly" miners moving into AI/HPC hosting (RIOT, CORZ, IREN). [[ai-tech/source-semianalysis-datacenter-delay-narrative-2026-06-18]] shows what that pivot looks like on the ground: CoreWeave's Denton campus is a Core Scientific site, and it was already slipping on redesigns, permits and a transformer explosion. [[finance/morningstar/source-morningstar-coreweave-debt-neocloud-ipo-2026-10-22]] now has CRWV's 2031 unsecured notes at 79 (≈16% yield), CDS "blown out", a Korean neocloud IPO down 32% on debut, an Australian one shelved, and a distressed investor calling CoreWeave "Exhibit One" for overlevered balance sheets. A miner whose new revenue is a lease to CoreWeave or a similar neocloud now carries that credit risk. Core Scientific's biggest tenant is CoreWeave, which tried to buy it in 2025 (outside knowledge; check before citing). There are two channels back to Fred's crypto. (1) If hosting leases fail, the converted power goes back to mining, which raises hashrate and lowers miner margins, and stressed miners sell BTC. That pressure is on top of the July drawdown already in [[crypto/source-morningstar-crypto-winter-2026-07-24]]. (2) The same piece lists CoreWeave's $4.2bn and Nebius's $5.75bn convertibles. MSTR, Fred's leveraged BTC proxy in [[finance/portfolio-overview]], funds itself through the same convertible market, so heavy convert losses on neoclouds would tighten MSTR's main funding channel. [[crypto/crypto-overview]] values BTC on a "digital scarcity" and macro-hedge story only. A "Concepts to Research" line on miner AI-hosting exposure (which listed miners lease to which neocloud, and for what share of revenue) would turn the Burry neocloud bear case into a named BTC risk.
